structure.text: Did the consignment leave the UK?
Yes / No / Consignment has been destroyed
Shown when 'Yes' (consignment left): Means of transport, Identification, Documentation, Date of departure, Exit BCP, Destination Country
Identification — hint: Flight number, vessel name or vehicle registration
Documentation — hint: Air Waybill, Bill of lading or ship manifest
Date of departure — hint: For example: 01 03 2017
Shown when 'No' (consignment did not leave): nested question 'Did the consignment reach the controlled destination?'
Did the consignment reach the controlled destination?
Shown when 'Consignment has been destroyed': Destruction date
To the best of my knowledge, the details provided are correct.
Animal and Plant Health Agency, New Haw, Woodham Lane, Addlestone, KT15 3NB, GB

govukComponents.usage: Top-level 'Did the consignment leave the UK?' (Yes/No/Consignment has been destroyed) with conditional reveals; nested 'Did the consignment reach the controlled destination?' (Yes/No)
Wraps each radio question and the two date-input groups; legend heading rendered as <h3>
Means of transport, Exit BCP (199 options, reference data), Destination Country (250 options, reference data)
Date of departure (leave-date), Destruction date (destruction-date) — each three text inputs day/month/year
Reason (why consignment did not reach controlled destination), rows=3
Reference-number caption inside H1, plus field hints on Identification, Documentation, Date of departure, Destruction date
Field labels for selects, text inputs, date sub-inputs and textarea

nonStandardPatterns.pattern: defra-datepicker / date-picker__container / date-picker__dialog / date-picker__date-table / date-picker__button__* / date-input--picker (data-module="accessible-datepicker")
nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: A custom JavaScript calendar-popup date picker (DEFRA's own widget) layered onto the standard govuk-date-input day/month/year text fields — adds a 'Choose date' icon button that opens a modal month grid.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: The GOV.UK Design System deliberately has no date-picker component; it recommends three plain text inputs. This is a bespoke widget with its own dialog, ARIA live region and month-navigation buttons that the new app would have to reimplement or drop.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: govuk-date-input (three text inputs, day/month/year) with no calendar popup — already present underneath; the new app can keep just the govuk-date-input and drop the custom picker.
nonStandardPatterns.evidence: trace 189085ad930266a48c024dc1d447e1c2055d6fe9 action 228 (classes: defra-datepicker, date-picker__dialog, aria-live-message, sr-only)

nonStandardPatterns.pattern: Two <h1> elements on one page (govuk-heading-xl 'Record control' and govuk-heading-l 'Declaration')
nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: The page renders a second <h1> ('Declaration') styled as heading-l, in addition to the main 'Record control' h1.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: Two h1s per page is an accessibility anti-pattern (one h1 per page). Combined with fieldset legends rendered as <h3> and no <h2>, the heading hierarchy skips levels.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: Single h1 per page; 'Declaration' should be an <h2> and the question legends <h2>/<h3> in a consistent order.

nonStandardPatterns.pattern: Reference number rendered as govuk-hint with govuk-!-font-size-27 inside the H1
nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: The consignment reference + version ('CHEDP.GB.2026.1526061 - V1') is a govuk-hint span inside the h1 with a hard-coded 27px font-size override, acting as a caption.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: IPAFFS does not use the standard govuk-caption-xl caption pattern; it hard-codes a font size and nests the caption inside the h1.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: govuk-caption-xl / govuk-caption-l above the h1 (the standard section-caption pattern).

nonStandardPatterns.pattern: Reason textarea label uses govuk-!-font-weight-bold instead of govuk-label--m
nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: The 'Reason' textarea label applies a bold font-weight utility rather than the standard medium label modifier used by the other fields on the page.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: Inconsistent label styling within the same page; minor deviation from the standard label size scale.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: govuk-label--m (as used by the sibling fields).
nonStandardPatterns.evidence: trace 189085ad930266a48c024dc1d447e1c2055d6fe9 action 228 (label class govuk-label govuk-label govuk-!-font-weight-bold for consignment-no-arrival-reason)

nonStandardPatterns.pattern: data-country-code attributes on <option> elements (Exit BCP, transport, country selects)
nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: Each select option carries a data-country-code attribute used by client-side JS (e.g. to filter Exit BCPs to GB).
nonStandardPatterns.concern: Custom data-attribute-driven client filtering; not part of a standard Design System component.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: Server-side filtered option lists sourced from a reference-data service; no client data attributes needed.

openQuestions: Legacy validation establishes that the top-level outcome is required; departure date is required on the Yes branch; destruction date is required on the destruction branch; other branch controls are optional in the old system. This is legacy policy and should be confirmed for the rebuild, particularly the surprising optional controlled-destination radio, Exit BCP and destination country.

Rendered CHED-P copy for identification/documentation conflicts with the CHED-P-gated legacy template: the trace confirms 'Identification' / 'Documentation' with short hints, while ipaffs-frontend-control/service/src/views/ov/consignmentLeave.html:54-94 specifies 'Transport identification' / 'Transport document reference' and expanded hints. Confirm which copy the rebuild should use; rendered values remain authoritative in the primary label/hint fields.

The top question offers three mutually exclusive outcomes (consignment left / did not leave / has been destroyed). 'Did the consignment reach the controlled destination?' is a nested sub-question revealed only under 'No'. Confirm the new app models this as one radio with conditional reveals vs. separate pages.

Exit BCP list (199 options) is heavily polluted with synthetic 'ABC Legal - <code>' test entries in this environment; the real production list is the named GB BCPs only. New app should source from the BCP reference-data service.

The declaration block (Name, Registered location, Date control added) is read-only pre-filled data about the signed-in inspector/officer, not user input — the new app needs the source of the officer's registered location.
This is the control-app (LVU/inspector) surface, journey position -1 (after the notification is submitted). Confirm it is in scope for the CHED-P rebuild vs. handled by a separate control service.

QA independently covers only consignment-leave = No, consignment-arrival = Yes and Submit control (page-objects/control/RecordControlPage.ts:6-15; workflows/notification/ched-p-workflows.ts:1271-1274). It has no locators or CHED-P assertions for the Yes/departure branch, destruction branch, arrival = No reason, transport type, identification, documentation, departure date, Exit BCP, destination country or destruction date; all of those definitions remain trace-confirmed but independently unasserted.
